title: Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2025
official_title: To direct the Secretary of Commerce to take actions necessary and appropriate to promote the competitiveness of the United States related to the deployment, use, application, and competitiveness of blockchain technology or other distributed ledger technology, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: The sponsor is a Republican in the Republican-majority House and the bill passed the House, and its rules of construction impose no obligation on private entities, limiting opposition. It carries only one cosponsor and now sits with the Senate Commerce Committee, so Senate floor time is uncertain.
summary: This bill makes the Secretary of Commerce the federal government's lead advisor on blockchain and distributed-ledger technology and sets up a Blockchain Deployment Program to promote its use. The program develops voluntary best practices, convenes advisory committees, and reports to Congress, but requires nothing of private companies.
brief: Directs the Commerce Department to lead a voluntary federal program promoting blockchain and distributed-ledger technology.

top_lines.headline: Commerce Department Blockchain Role
subs: Names the Commerce Secretary as the President's principal blockchain advisor
Creates a Blockchain Deployment Program in the Commerce Department
The program sunsets 7 years after enactment

top_lines.headline: Blockchain Advisory Committees
subs: Advisory committees must be established within 180 days
Membership spans industry, academia, cybersecurity, and rural stakeholders

top_lines.headline: Best Practices and Reporting
subs: Commerce develops and shares voluntary blockchain best practices
Public report to Congress within 2 years, then annually

sections.label: Section 3 - Department of Commerce Leadership on Blockchain

items.main: Designates the Secretary of Commerce as the President's principal advisor on blockchain and distributed-ledger technology and creates a Blockchain Deployment Program.
items.detail: The Secretary must develop policies on issues including decentralized identity, cybersecurity, key storage, artificial intelligence, fraud reduction, and supply-chain resiliency, and examine how federal agencies use and could adopt the technology. The Blockchain Deployment Program terminates 7 years after enactment.

items.main: Requires the Secretary to establish blockchain advisory committees within 180 days, with broad governmental and nongovernmental membership.
items.detail: Members include federal agency representatives and nongovernmental stakeholders such as infrastructure operators, application developers, small to large businesses, think tanks and academia, cybersecurity experts, rural stakeholders, and artists and content creators. The Secretary also develops and disseminates voluntary best practices on an ongoing basis.

items.main: States that nothing in the section requires a private entity to share information, seek assistance, implement recommendations, or adopt the best practices.
items.detail: The rules of construction make participation and adoption voluntary for private entities. In carrying out the section the Secretary must consult stakeholders, develop standardized terminology, and support open-source infrastructure.

items.main: Requires a public report to Congress within 2 years of enactment and annually thereafter on the program's activities.
items.detail: The Secretary must post the report on the Commerce Department website and submit it to the House Energy and Commerce Committee and the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee. It must describe the Secretary's activities, any recommendations for additional legislation, and emerging risks and long-term trends.

underreported.summary: Bars construing the section to require any private entity to share information, request assistance, implement a recommendation, or adopt the best practices.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill is titled around deploying blockchain, but its operative effect on the private sector is entirely voluntary rather than a mandate.

gaps: The bill directs Commerce to lead on blockchain competitiveness but authorizes no funding for the Blockchain Deployment Program or advisory committees.
The bill establishes advisory committees but sets no limit on their number, size, or members' terms.
The bill directs examination of federal agencies' blockchain use but sets no standards or requirements for that use.
The bill requires development of standardized terminology but does not say who resolves disputes over definitions.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Cammack
featured_quotes.text: This bill is about far more than emerging technology. It is about securing America's future, economically, strategically, and technologically, in an increasingly digital world. Blockchain technology is not a passing trend. It is a foundational innovation that is reshaping how we think about security, identity, data integrity, and commerce. From supply chains and finance to healthcare and identity management, blockchain is transforming the way our systems function. Mr. Speaker, we are at a crossroads.

added: The Secretary of Commerce as the President's principal advisor on blockchain and distributed-ledger technology
A Blockchain Deployment Program in the Commerce Department that sunsets 7 years after enactment
Blockchain advisory committees, to be established within 180 days
A public report to Congress within 2 years of enactment and annually thereafter
